Thanks for the call today, Stephanie — good coverage from both sides. Per our discussion, I'm sharing our internal one-pager and a rough list of metrics we care about (attached: cedartech_initial_scope.pdf). High level asks from CedarTech: low-latency inference for multitenant documents, token-cost transparency, and audit logs for PII flows.

Next steps we discussed:
- Redwood to propose a POC acceptance matrix (success criteria + owners)
- Redwood engineering to confirm time-to-first-token for our 2k-document sample
- CedarTech to circulate an exec slot for a final readout (week of Mar 22 preferred)

Questions for Redwood: who will own the live evaluation monitoring? Is that Redwood CS or CedarTech ops?

Head of Platform Engineering
CedarTech

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap / next steps — proposed POC acceptance matrix

Hi Lena — thanks for the doc and for the clear priorities. Attached are two artifacts for the POC: a proposed evaluation matrix (cedartech_poc_eval_matrix.xlsx) and our POC playbook (redwood_poc_playbook.pdf). Key items summarized below.

POC scope (2-week hands-on trial):
- Dataset: 2k representative customer docs (you provide S3 link)
- Workloads: synchronous chat-style generation (avg 120 tokens) + batch embeddings for search
- Models: rdx-3b-quant (primary), rdx-7b-fallback for quality checks

Proposed acceptance criteria (owners in parens):
1) Latency: median request latency < 150ms for chat API at 95th pct (Rishi)
2) Quality: end-to-end similarity score >= 0.78 vs baseline (CedarTech SME)
3) Cost: token unit cost <= $0.0015 (Aditya)
4) Observability: real-time token and latency dashboards + audit log retention 90 days (Neha + CedarTech ops)
5) Reliability: 99.5% success rate over 24h stability window (Rishi)

Owners / touchpoints:
- Redwood SE (Rishi): infra setup and baseline latency tests
- Redwood Ops (Aditya): batching and cost knobs; run unit-cost sim
- Redwood CS (Neha): monitoring dashboard and daily check-ins during POC
- CedarTech (Lena / Mark): dataset & business-quality review

Schedule (target):
- Week 1: infra onboarding + small synthetic tests
- Week 2: full-sweep evaluation + quality review; final readout the following week

Attachments include a compact acceptance matrix with pass/fail thresholds and a seeded test set example. Please review and let me know your edits; I can update the matrix and share a HubSpot deal checklist and a draft SOW for procurement.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com

Attachments: cedartech_poc_eval_matrix.xlsx; redwood_poc_playbook.pdf

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@cedartech.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap / next steps — proposed POC acceptance matrix

Quick technical clarifications from my side:
- For the 2k documents, please confirm average token length (Lena) — I'll size batch windows accordingly.
- We'll run two latency profiles: cold-start (no KV cache) and warmed cache; acceptance should use warmed numbers but both reported.
- Will run an initial 2-hour stability pass before full-sweep; if we miss 99.5% success rate we'll do a 12-hour follow-up with increased retry/backoff.

Availability for infra onboarding: Wed 17 Mar and Thu 18 Mar mornings PST.

-Rishi
Principal SE, Redwood
